title: TENIR-Gov: Governance Middleware for AI-Enabled Operational Systems
description:
TENIR-Gov is an open-source governance middleware that sits between decision-producing AI agents and downstream execution environments. It enforces explicit policies, validates operational intents through a neuro-symbolic grammar layer, and persists every governance decision in a cryptographically verifiable Merkle-based audit ledger — independently of any underlying AI model.

The 5.7 line extends published 5.6.1 with: neuro-symbolic validation (LALR(1) grammar + optional LLM fine-tuning), a deterministic policy engine (frozen dataclass contract), a graph-based policy store (Neo4j 5.x), a Merkle epoch audit ledger, an administrative governance plane, a polymorphic UI surface contract, ledger migration tooling, two-kernel composition with HOLD/ESCALATE lifecycle, post-execution assessment (τ⁻¹ partial tau inversion + EVP), a hardened I8 aggregate budget invariant with governor-owned reservation, and CAVE aligned to the epistemic doctrine (Control / Aim / Veto / Epistemics).

5.7.6, the single-host pilot line, hardens 5.7.0 (the 5.7.5 candidate was merged but not published): no favorable default for an unmeasured axis (option_space included), no conclusive veto masked by an invalid measure, no failure after dispatch without a persisted proof of non-execution that the runtime has authenticated, a FLAG that admits only under declared and acknowledged conditions, a mandate re-validated before dispatch, and a declarable HOLD bound (τ_K) that refuses alone.
notes: 5.7.7 release metadata, written in the source before archiving (the publication status, publication date and version DOI of a release are those shown on its Zenodo record): single-host pilot line, continuing the fail-closed hardening of 5.7.0 and 5.7.6; 5.7.5 is an unpublished candidate. 5.7.7 adds, on top of the published 5.7.6 (the full list is under "Upgrading from 5.7.6" in `CHANGELOG.md`): `DualKernelCompositionClient` refuses to construct unless its policy declares τ_K (`hold_tau_k_seconds` and `hold_tau_k_source`); an absent mandatory measure holds unless a conclusive veto governs; a measure outside the kernel's declared domain, a measure that is not a number and a malformed request are rejected explicitly as `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, instead of being held or vetoed; the decision ledger is verified in full under the quarantine gate before every dispatch claim, in this process; the ledger is thread-safe and its state is taken at one instant; and one audit entry is written per ledger-integrity incident. Its declared limits are listed release by release in `CHANGELOG.md`, and it is a bounded-guarantee single-host technical release, not a REG-qualified one. FM-20 remains open; PySyncObj transport is restricted to explicitly declared development/test environments with loopback-only peers. Production and physical multi-host Raft are unsupported. DOIs: the concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21264802 identifies the all-versions series and resolves to the latest version; each archived release has its own version DOI, assigned by Zenodo when the release is archived, which therefore cannot appear in that release's source metadata. Version DOIs of published releases: 5.7.6, 10.5281/zenodo.24408212; 5.7.0, 10.5281/zenodo.23623842; 5.6.1, 10.5281/zenodo.23493054; 5.6.0, 10.5281/zenodo.23463289 (its Zenodo version field reads 5.5.0). 5.7.5 was never published and has no DOI. Corrections to earlier metadata: 10.5281/zenodo.21277138 is the archive of GitHub release V1.0.4 (2026-07-09), not of v5.6.0; 10.5281/zenodo.21264803 is the first version of this software series (archive of GitHub release V1.0.1, 2026-07-08), not an article.
